title: A New Lunar Crater: McGetchin
explanation:
# The Moon's Rare Cosmic Collision

A whale-sized space rock slammed into the Moon between April and May 2024, carving out a crater the size of two soccer fields—a cosmic impact so rare that astronomers expect to witness only one like it every 132 years. NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter captured stunning before-and-after images revealing not just the visible crater, but a sprawling cold zone surrounding it, where the impact's shock wave fluffed up the Moon's fine dust into an insulating blanket that can't hold heat, teaching us invaluable lessons about how celestial impacts reshape planetary surfaces and reminding us how fortunate we are to have Earth's protective atmosphere.
